title: SPA fallback can read files outside the frontend directory
reasoning: The catch-all route joins the URL path directly onto FRONTEND_DIR and serves the result if it exists. Encoded dot segments such as /%2e%2e/pyproject.toml are decoded by Starlette into ../pyproject.toml, so the Path join can escape the frontend directory and FileResponse can return arbitrary readable files adjacent to or above the frontend build when the frontend routes are enabled.
reproduction: With the same route pattern, TestClient preserves encoded traversal: GET /%2e%2e/pyproject.toml produced full_path '../pyproject.toml' and resolved to frontend/../pyproject.toml, which exists and is_file=True.
recommendation: Resolve the candidate path and verify it remains under FRONTEND_DIR.resolve() before serving, or delegate static file serving to Starlette StaticFiles for all static assets. Reject traversal attempts with 404 before constructing FileResponse.
whyTestsDoNotAlreadyCoverThis: No linked tests cover the frontend-build branch. The existing health/root tests import the app without a built frontend index, so serve_spa is not registered.
suggestedRegressionTest: Create a temporary frontend build with index.html, register the app or extracted route against it, and assert GET '/%2e%2e/pyproject.toml' returns 404 while a real frontend asset under the directory still returns 200.
minimumFixScope: The direct-file branch inside serve_spa in app/main.py.
